topic: How does linear search find 4 in 7, 3, 9, 4, 6?
title: Linear Search

scenes.narration: Linear search is the most direct way to find something: check the first value, then the next, and so on, until you find the target or run out. Here the target is 4.
scenes.caption: Look at each value in turn

scenes.narration: Index 0 holds 7, which is not 4, so we move on.
scenes.caption: check index 0: 7

scenes.narration: Index 1 holds 3. Still not the target.
scenes.caption: check index 1: 3

scenes.narration: Index 2 holds 9. The array is not sorted, so we cannot skip anything; we keep going.
scenes.caption: check index 2: 9

scenes.narration: Index 3 holds 4, the target. The search stops after 4 checks.
scenes.caption: check index 3: found 4

scenes.narration: Linear search needed 4 checks here. If the target were missing, it would have checked all 5 values before giving up.
scenes.caption: Summary
points: Check values one by one from the start
Works on any array, sorted or not
O(n) checks in the worst case

quiz.question: Linear search looks for 6 in 5, 2, 8, 1 and checks every value. Was 6 found?
quiz.explanation: 6 is not in the array, so all four checks fail.

quiz.question: Linear search looks for 1 in 4, 8, 1, 5. At which index does it stop?
quiz.explanation: 1 sits at index 2, the third value checked.
